title: Salvation through Faith Alone
definition: Salvation through Faith Alone teaches that sinners receive justification and salvation by trusting in Christ, not by earning righteousness.
summary: Salvation through Faith Alone teaches that sinners receive Christ and His benefits by trusting Him, not by works.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the object of saving faith and the only ground of acceptance before God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Faith alone identifies the empty hand that receives Christ. It is not a meritorious work, a vague optimism, or mere agreement with facts. Saving faith rests on Jesus Himself—His person, promise, death, and resurrection.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people either trust themselves or despair over themselves. Faith alone redirects confidence away from the sinner and toward the Savior. It protects the Gospel from both legalism and self-made spirituality.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask where your confidence truly rests when you think about standing before God. Call people to trust Christ, not to trust the sincerity of a moment or the weight of their works. Strengthen faith by looking steadily at Jesus.
